topics.concept: Customer acquisition cost divides total sales and marketing spend by the number of new customers won in the same period. It is the price tag on growth and must be read alongside lifetime value to know whether new customers pay back. Breaking it down by channel shows which programs buy customers cheaply and which burn budget.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded monthly spend and win data per channel, computes blended and per-channel CAC, and flags channels whose CAC exceeds a payback threshold.

key_params.marketing_spend: total marketing cost for the period
key_params.new_customers: count of customers acquired in the period
key_params.sales_spend: total sales cost allocated to new business

topics.name: Customer Acquisition Cost Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Marketing and sales leaders use CAC to budget campaigns and decide where to invest the next dollar of acquisition spend.

topics.concept: Lifetime value estimates the gross profit a customer generates across the whole relationship. A cohort version groups customers by signup month and projects each cohort's value from its observed retention curve rather than a single blended average. This exposes whether newer cohorts are healthier or weaker than older ones.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded cohort revenue curves with decaying retention, fits a retention model per cohort, and reports projected LTV alongside realized-to-date LTV.

key_params.arpa: average revenue per account per month

topics.name: Cohort Lifetime Value Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Subscription businesses compare cohort LTV against acquisition cost to set allowable CAC and pricing strategy.

topics.concept: Logo churn counts customers lost as a share of the starting base, while revenue churn measures dollars lost, net of expansion. Revenue churn tells the truer story because losing one enterprise account hurts more than losing ten tiny ones. Tracking both monthly exposes whether churn is a volume problem or a value problem.
topics.data_idea: Simulates a seeded customer base with contract values, monthly churn events, and expansion, then computes logo churn, gross revenue churn, and net revenue churn per month.

key_params.starting_mrr: monthly recurring revenue at month one

topics.name: Churn Rate Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Customer success teams watch churn dashboards to trigger save plays before renewal dates arrive.

topics.concept: Net promoter score comes from a single 0 to 10 question: promoters score 9 or 10, passives 7 or 8, detractors 6 or below, and NPS is promoters minus detractors. The number is simple, but its power is in the trend and the verbatim themes behind it. Simulating responses shows how sample size and sentiment mix move the score.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded survey responses with score distributions and free-text themes, computes NPS per segment and month, and shows confidence bands by sample size.

key_params.respondents: number of survey responses to simulate
key_params.trend_months: months of trend history to generate

topics.name: Net Promoter Score Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Product and CX teams track NPS quarterly and tie detractor themes to roadmap fixes.

topics.concept: A retention heatmap lays signup cohorts on rows and months-since-signup on columns, coloring each cell by the share still active. Healthy products show columns that flatten; leaky ones fade left to right. The heatmap turns a wall of churn numbers into a pattern anyone can read in seconds.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded per-cohort retention matrices with improving or degrading shapes, renders the heatmap, and highlights cohorts that deviate from the baseline curve.

key_params.periods: months of retention tracked per cohort
key_params.retention_shape: decay curve family for the simulation

topics.name: Cohort Retention Heatmap
topics.real_world_use: Growth teams use retention heatmaps to judge whether onboarding changes actually improved stickiness.

topics.concept: A pipeline dashboard aggregates every open opportunity by stage, weighting each by its close probability to show expected bookings. Stage conversion rates reveal where deals stall, and aging buckets show which opportunities are quietly dying. It is the earliest warning system a revenue leader has.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded opportunities with stage, value, age, and owner, then computes weighted pipeline, conversion between stages, and stalled-deal alerts.

key_params.aging_buckets: day ranges that flag stale deals
key_params.stages: named pipeline stages with win probabilities

topics.name: Sales Pipeline Dashboard
topics.real_world_use: Sales managers run weekly forecast calls off pipeline dashboards to decide which deals need executive help.

topics.concept: Subscription businesses live on a small set of recurring metrics: MRR, ARR, new versus expansion versus churned MRR, and the quick ratio that weighs growth against loss. Watching them together each month shows whether growth is real or borrowed from next quarter. A monitor that alerts on sudden shifts beats a spreadsheet reviewed quarterly.
topics.data_idea: Simulates monthly MRR movements across new, expansion, contraction, and churn buckets, computes the quick ratio and net retention, and raises alerts on threshold breaches.

key_params.alert_threshold: change size that triggers an alert

topics.name: SaaS Metrics Monitor
topics.real_world_use: Finance and RevOps teams monitor these metrics monthly to validate forecasts and catch churn spikes early.

topics.concept: The magic number divides net new ARR by sales and marketing spend to measure how efficiently spend converts into recurring revenue. Above 1.0 the engine is efficient; below 0.75 it suggests spending should slow until efficiency improves. It is a blunt instrument, so it works best averaged over several quarters to smooth seasonality.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded quarterly ARR movements and spend series, computes the magic number per quarter and trailing averages, and labels efficiency bands.

key_params.net_new_arr: ARR added minus ARR churned per quarter
key_params.sm_spend: sales and marketing spend per quarter

topics.name: SaaS Magic Number Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Boards use the magic number to judge whether a company should pour fuel on sales or fix the go-to-market engine first.

topics.concept: Net burn is cash out minus cash in per month, and runway is cash on hand divided by net burn: the months until the money runs out. Gross burn shows spending pace ignoring revenue, which matters when revenue is lumpy. Every startup plan is really a bet that the next milestone lands before the runway ends.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded cash trajectory with hiring-driven cost steps and revenue ramps, computes gross and net burn, and projects the runway end date with a sensitivity band.
topics.name: Burn Rate and Runway Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Startup CFOs report burn and runway to the board every month to time fundraising.

topics.concept: Gross margin is revenue minus cost of goods sold, divided by revenue: what is left after delivering the product, before overhead. Tracking it by product line shows which lines earn their keep and which subsidize the rest. A falling blended margin often means the mix shifted toward lower-margin business, not that costs rose.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded revenue and COGS per product line, computes margins and the mix effect, and flags lines dragging the blended margin down.
topics.name: Gross Margin Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Product finance teams use margin analysis to price new tiers and decide which products to invest in.

topics.concept: Net revenue retention starts with a cohort's revenue, subtracts churn and contraction, adds expansion, and divides by the starting figure. Above 100 percent means the base grows even without new sales, which is the hallmark of product-led growth. It rewards both keeping customers and selling them more.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded revenue movements per cohort across churn, contraction, and expansion, then reports gross and net retention with the expansion contribution isolated.
topics.name: Net Revenue Retention Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Investors treat net revenue retention as a core health metric when valuing subscription companies.

topics.concept: A lead funnel counts how many visitors become leads, how many leads become qualified, and how many qualified become customers. Each step has a conversion rate, and the weakest step is where fixing leaks pays most. The funnel also sets the top-of-funnel volume needed to hit a bookings target.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded lead records flowing through stages with probabilistic conversion, computes per-stage rates, and back-solves required top-of-funnel volume for a target.

key_params.top_volume: visitors or leads entering the top

topics.name: Lead Conversion Funnel
topics.real_world_use: Demand generation teams size campaigns from funnel math so marketing delivers enough pipeline for sales.

topics.concept: Stickiness divides daily active users by monthly active users: the share of the monthly audience that shows up on a typical day. Social and messaging products target 50 percent or more; utilities are happy far lower. Tracking it by cohort shows whether new features pull people back more often.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded daily logins per user with habit-forming return probabilities, computes DAU, MAU, stickiness, and cohort stickiness curves.
topics.name: DAU MAU Stickiness Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Product teams track stickiness weekly as the leading indicator of engagement health.

topics.concept: Coverage divides total open pipeline by the quota or target for the period. A ratio near three is the classic comfort zone: enough pipeline that even with losses the target is reachable. Coverage below target with weeks left in the quarter is the signal to generate pipeline or cut the forecast.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded pipeline snapshot per rep and segment, computes coverage ratios against quota, and projects the shortfall under historical win rates.
topics.name: Pipeline Coverage Ratio Monitor
topics.real_world_use: Revenue leaders review coverage in weekly forecast meetings to decide whether the number is safe.

topics.concept: CAC payback divides acquisition cost by the monthly gross profit per customer: the months until a customer repays what it cost to win them. Shorter payback means capital recycles faster and growth needs less funding. Segmenting payback by channel and plan tier shows where capital works hardest.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded CAC and margin data per segment, computes payback months, and ranks segments by capital efficiency with threshold flags.

key_params.target_months: payback ceiling for a healthy segment

topics.name: CAC Payback Period Model
topics.real_world_use: CFOs use payback by segment to allocate acquisition budget toward the fastest-returning channels.

topics.concept: The LTV to CAC ratio asks whether a customer is worth several times what it cost to acquire them. Around three is the rule of thumb: lower suggests overspending on acquisition or weak monetization, much higher can mean under-investing in growth. The ratio only means something when both halves are measured on the same cohorts.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded LTV and CAC per segment with cohort alignment, computes the ratio with uncertainty bands, and benchmarks each segment against the rule-of-thumb bands.

key_params.cac_window: period over which CAC is measured

topics.name: LTV to CAC Ratio Dashboard
topics.real_world_use: Growth teams use the ratio to set maximum bids and channel budgets in performance marketing.

topics.concept: Win-loss analysis codes every closed deal with why it was won or lost: price, features, timing, incumbent, or champion strength. Aggregating codes by segment reveals whether losses cluster around one fixable cause. A classifier trained on deal attributes can then flag at-risk open deals that look like past losses.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded closed deals with attributes and coded outcomes, tallies win rates by code and segment, and trains a simple classifier to score open deals for loss risk.

key_params.deals: number of closed deals in history
key_params.features: deal attributes used by the classifier

topics.name: Win Loss Deal Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Product marketing uses win-loss findings to sharpen battlecards and prioritize roadmap gaps competitors exploit.

topics.concept: Quota attainment divides actual bookings by assigned quota per rep, team, and region. It is the fairest scoreboard because it normalizes for territory size. Tracking attainment distribution, not just the average, shows whether the plan is realistic or only the top few can hit it.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded bookings per rep with realistic skew, computes attainment percentages, and charts the distribution to flag unrealistic quota setting.

key_params.quota: quota assigned per rep or team

topics.name: Quota Attainment Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Sales operations reviews attainment quarterly to calibrate next year's quotas and compensation plans.

topics.concept: Sales cycle length measures days from qualified opportunity to close, and it lengthens with deal size and committee buying. Segmenting cycle length by segment, source, and stage dwell time shows exactly where days pile up. Shortening the slowest stage moves revenue forward without adding headcount.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded deal histories with stage entry and exit dates, computes cycle length distributions per segment, and identifies the highest-dwell stage.

key_params.segments: segments to compare cycle length across
key_params.stage_names: stages whose dwell time is measured

topics.name: Sales Cycle Length Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Sales leaders use cycle analysis to set close plans and to coach reps on stages where deals stall.

topics.concept: A health score blends product usage, support tickets, payment behavior, and engagement into one 0 to 100 number per account. The weights come from history: signals that preceded past churns earn more weight. Scores drive playbooks, so green accounts get expansion offers while red ones get save plans.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded account signals with known churn outcomes, fits signal weights from historical churn, and scores accounts into green, yellow, and red bands.

key_params.signals: usage, support, billing, and engagement inputs

topics.name: Customer Health Scorer
topics.real_world_use: Customer success platforms surface health scores so CSMs prioritize the accounts most likely to churn.

topics.concept: Forecast accuracy compares predicted revenue against actuals each period, and bias shows whether misses run consistently high or low. A forecaster who is always optimistic needs calibration, not just a better model. Tracking accuracy by segment reveals whether the problem is the method or one unpredictable region.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded actuals with trend and noise, produces forecasts from competing methods, and scores each on error, bias, and directional accuracy.
topics.name: Revenue Forecast Accuracy Tracker
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams track forecast accuracy to earn credibility with the board and to improve planning models.

topics.concept: An SLA monitor checks every ticket against its response and resolution targets by priority. Breach rate, mean time to resolve, and backlog age together show whether the queue is under control. Alerting on breaches in real time matters more than a monthly report because SLAs are measured in hours.
topics.data_idea: Simulates a seeded ticket stream with arrival times, priorities, and handle times, then computes breach rates, MTTR, and backlog aging with live alerts.

key_params.priorities: priority levels with their SLA targets

topics.name: Support SLA Monitor
topics.real_world_use: Support operations teams watch SLA dashboards to staff shifts and escalate before contracts are breached.

topics.concept: Activation rate is the share of new signups that reach the product's key first value moment, like sending a first invoice or inviting a teammate. It is the bridge between acquisition and retention: users who never activate cannot become retained. Defining activation crisply is half the work; the rest is removing friction on the path to it.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded signup journeys with drop-off at each onboarding step, computes activation rate by channel and week, and pinpoints the highest-friction step.
topics.name: Activation Rate Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Onboarding teams run experiments against activation rate because it predicts long-term retention.

topics.concept: Gross revenue retention caps each account at 100 percent, so it measures pure keeping power without expansion masking churn. Net retention allows expansion above 100, measuring growth within the base. Watching the gap between them shows whether growth comes from selling more to happy customers or merely from replacing leavers.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded account revenue with churn, contraction, and expansion events, then computes gross and net retention and decomposes net into its moving parts.
topics.name: Gross vs Net Retention Monitor
topics.real_world_use: SaaS CFOs report both numbers because gross retention reveals churn that net retention can hide.

topics.concept: A leaderboard ranks reps on attainment, pipeline created, and activity quality, updated as deals close. Public rankings motivate, but the design matters: weighting only closed revenue encourages sandbagging, while including pipeline rewards future building. The best boards celebrate both hunters and farmers.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded rep performance across bookings, pipeline, and activity, computes a weighted score, and renders a ranked board with trend arrows.
topics.name: Sales Rep Leaderboard
topics.real_world_use: Sales floors display leaderboards to drive friendly competition and spotlight top performers.

topics.concept: Attribution assigns credit for a conversion across the touches a buyer saw: first touch, last touch, linear, or position-based. No model is true, but comparing models shows which channels assist versus close. The honest use is directional budget shifts, not claiming exact ROI per touch.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded multi-touch buyer journeys with channel touches and conversions, applies several attribution models, and contrasts channel credit under each.
topics.name: Marketing Attribution Model
topics.real_world_use: Marketing teams use attribution comparisons to rebalance spend between awareness and conversion channels.

topics.concept: Upsell rate measures how often existing customers buy more: higher tiers, more seats, or add-on products. It is cheaper than new acquisition and signals product satisfaction. Tracking it by cohort and CSM shows whether expansion is a repeatable motion or a few heroic saves.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded accounts with expansion offers and acceptances, computes attach rates by offer and cohort, and estimates expansion revenue per eligible account.
topics.name: Upsell and Cross-sell Rate Monitor
topics.real_world_use: Account management teams set expansion targets from upsell benchmarks by segment.

topics.concept: Cost per ticket divides total support cost, including staff, tools, and overhead, by resolved tickets. It falls with deflection through self-service and rises when complex issues need senior agents. Segmenting by channel and issue type shows where automation pays back fastest.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded cost model with agent salaries, handle times, and ticket mix, then computes cost per ticket by channel and issue type with deflection scenarios.
topics.name: Support Cost per Ticket Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Support leaders justify knowledge-base and chatbot investments with cost-per-ticket math.

topics.concept: Not all acquired customers are equal: one channel may bring cheap signups that churn fast while another brings expensive ones that stay for years. Comparing LTV by acquisition channel, adjusted for CAC, reveals true channel quality. Clustering channels by behavior uncovers groups that deserve different nurture tracks.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded cohorts per channel with distinct retention and spend profiles, computes LTV and LTV-to-CAC per channel, and clusters channels by customer behavior.
topics.name: Channel Cohort LTV Comparator
topics.real_world_use: Performance marketers shift budgets toward channels whose customers, not clicks, are most valuable.

topics.concept: A north star metric is the single number that best captures the core value customers get, like messages sent or projects completed. Every team aligns its work to moving it. The tracker plots the metric daily with its key input drivers so everyone sees whether the company is actually delivering more value.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded daily series for a configurable north star plus its driver metrics, then shows correlations between driver moves and north star moves.

key_params.drivers: input metrics that move the north star

topics.name: North Star Metric Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Product-led companies review the north star in weekly all-hands to keep every team pointed the same way.
